correctness.rationale: Checked the down-set open/up-set closure convention and all v_{i,epsilon}<f_s iff epsilon=s_i incidences. An incident minimal vertex dominates each maximal facet in the closure-meeting graph; dually an incident facet dominates each minimal vertex in the inseparability graph, by inclusion of closed neighborhoods. Standard elementary flag-complex collapses then remove those dominated vertices without altering integral homotopy. Remaining vertices give graph K_{2,...,2} with m antipodal coordinate pairs, hence Cl=(S^0)^{*m}=S^(m-1); remaining facets give complete graph on 2^m sign words except 2^(m-1) antipodal edges, hence sphere S^(2^(m-1)-1). The Dowker complex allows at most one sign in each coordinate, giving another S^(m-1), and Cameron–Kumar Theorem 9.2(a) identifies the genuine nerves. Independently rebuilt the complete up/down incidence and verified both proposed neighborhood dominations for m=3,4,5, plus reduced opposite-pair formulas for m=3..6. Finite checks are corroboration, not the all-m proof.

value.rationale: Replacing a joint-intersection nerve by the clique complex of its one-skeleton is an important and sometimes invalid computational simplification. The canonical vertex–facet cross-polytope incidence family provides an unrestricted explicit dual counterexample where both flag completions remain spheres yet differ by an exponential dimension gap, rather than a trivial collapse to a point.

limitations: Only the two-rank vertex–facet incidence poset, not the entire cross-polytope face poset or its own weak homotopy type; finite check m<=6 cannot prove all m.
